texts: mixed: the sky-cat group, the visible state, the cliff-spire location, the morning and the per-member distribution all land, but the date does not — 'day 60 of Year 1' is recorded as a day-of-month numbered 60, so it is indistinguishable from an ordinary calendar date and two day-of-year dates in the same year will not be ordered against each other by the reasoner. If your calendar has month names, date it with a month plus a day inside that month: 'On the <n>th of <month-name>, Year 1, about four sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning.' Keep 'about' — the hedge is recorded as written, and dropping it would widen the claim.

mixed: the count, the cliff-spires and the morning land, but 'in a normal autumn' is read as one particular autumn that exists and happens to be normal, so the sentence is stored as a single observation rather than the typical baseline you mean — which is exactly the value the drought comparison has to be measured against. Move the typicality into an adverb, where it becomes a graded generic instead of a specific autumn: 'In autumn about ten sky-cats are normally visible on the cliff-spires in the morning.'

good. 'a handful' is a recognized vague-quantity phrase, 'for two weeks' becomes a duration on the visibility state itself, and that reified state is the anchor the following sentences should be pointing back at.

mixed: the hunting event, the sky-cat group, the Cliff Path and the per-member distribution are all fine, but 'in those two weeks' has no licensed time filler — the translator invented a bare span symbol that is never even said to be a stretch of time, and put that in the time slot, so the hunting is anchored to nothing the reasoner can use. Point at the two-week visibility the passage already states, which is a real eventuality and can carry a 'while': 'A handful of sky-cats had hunted on the Cliff Path while those sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires.'

mixed: the molting and its distribution to the individual cats are right, but 'in those two weeks' lands on that same invented, classless span symbol, so the molting gets no usable time anchor either. Same fix — tie it to the stated stretch of visibility: 'A handful of sky-cats had molted while those sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires.'

mixed: Tessa, the collecting, the feathers and the daily recurrence land, but two things break — 'during those two weeks' nests the collecting inside the invented span symbol rather than inside a real eventuality, and 'twelve feathers per morning' has no single carrier for a quantity-per-occasion. Both clear up if the rate is written as a plain per-morning habit and the span as the stated visibility: 'Tessa Brae collected about twelve feathers each morning while those sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires.'

mixed: this hits both earlier problems at once — 'in a normal autumn' asserts one particular normal autumn instead of stating the typical case, and 'per morning' again has no licensed rate carrier, which matters because this line is the baseline the twelve-a-morning figure is compared with. Write the typicality as an adverb and the rate as a per-morning habit: 'In autumn Tessa Brae normally collects about thirty-five feathers each morning.'
